AMR_STUDY: The study explicitly selects for ESBL-producing, ciprofloxacin-resistant, or carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae using selective culture/screening — AMR-selective screening, not routine all-comers surveillance; graded amr. AMR_TARGET: Three distinct resistance phenotypes are targeted simultaneously (ESBL/3GC, carbapenem/CPE, ciprofloxacin/fluoroquinolone), so no single amr_target value can cover all 84 deposited samples — graded partial, value null. AMR_METHOD: Graded ast_result because the selection criteria ('ESBL-producing', 'ciprofloxacin-resistant', 'carbapenemase-producing') are all phenotypic characterisations consistent with selective agar culture and AST confirmation; no PCR-gene-presence language is used, though the paper (not available) would confirm this. COHORT_AGE: Study explicitly includes both adult patients and infants (young children) → mixed. COUNTRY: Title states 'in The Netherlands'; description notes 'Dutch-Belgian border' but this characterises the study region rather than indicating samples from Belgium — Netherlands assigned as whole-project value. ISOLATION_SOURCE: 'Gut or rectal carriage' screening in all subjects (humans and animals) implies rectal swab as the predominant specimen; applied whole-project. HOST: Multiple host species (human, broiler chicken, weaned pig) with no evidence that any single species accounts for ≥95% of the 84 samples — applies_whole_project false. raw.notes: SIZING: All 84 ENA samples are Klebsiella (ena_taxon_samples = ena_total_samples = 84); no paper is available to compare against. AMR_STUDY: The study explicitly selects for ESBL-producing, ciprofloxacin-resistant, or carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae using selective culture/screening — AMR-selective screening, not routine all-comers surveillance; graded amr. AMR_TARGET: Three distinct resistance phenotypes are targeted simultaneously (ESBL/3GC, carbapenem/CPE, ciprofloxacin/fluoroquinolone), so no single amr_target value can cover all 84 deposited samples — graded partial, value null. AMR_METHOD: Graded ast_result because the selection criteria ('ESBL-producing', 'ciprofloxacin-resistant', 'carbapenemase-producing') are all phenotypic characterisations consistent with selective agar culture and AST confirmation; no PCR-gene-presence language is used, though the paper (not available) would confirm this. STUDY_SETTING: Medical centres = hospital; long-term healthcare facilities, daycare centres, and farms (non-human) = community per rubric → mixed. COHORT_AGE: Study explicitly includes both adult patients and infants (young children) → mixed. COUNTRY: Title states 'in The Netherlands'; description notes 'Dutch-Belgian border' but this characterises the study region rather than indicating samples from Belgium — Netherlands assigned as whole-project value. ISOLATION_SOURCE: 'Gut or rectal carriage' screening in all subjects (humans and animals) implies rectal swab as the predominant specimen; applied whole-project. HOST: Multiple host species (human, broiler chicken, weaned pig) with no evidence that any single species accounts for ≥95% of the 84 samples — applies_whole_project false. No collection dates are given beyond 'a one-year period'. A paper for the i-4-1-Health study almost certainly exists and should be retrieved to confirm amr_method, amr_target per-sample breakdown, and collection date range.

notes: ENA count (73) matches paper exactly: 75 isolates found, 2 reclassified as Citrobacter and excluded, leaving 73 Klebsiella genomes deposited under PRJEB56668 — 100% paper coverage, all study-level attributes gradeable. All isolates are from Italian artisanal food production facilities (salami and cheese), a non-human, non-hospital source → community. Selection criterion was purely microbiological (all morphologically typical Klebsiella colonies identified by biochemical test and PCR from food and food-production environments), not AMR-based → surveillance; AST was performed post-selection and the vast majority of isolates were susceptible. amr_target and amr_method are not applicable. All isolates originate from the food production chain context, so host = food applies across the whole project.

notes: SIZING: ENA=54 matches paper exactly: 9 parental clinical isolates + 5 PAP-selected colistin-resistant mutants per parental = 45 mutants; 9+45=54. Paper coverage = 100%. STUDY_TYPE: Classified experimental_evolution because 45/54 (83%) deposited sequences are in vitro-selected colistin-resistant mutants derived by culturing clinical isolates on colistin-containing agar (PAP assay), constituting deliberate antibiotic-pressure selection of resistant derivatives that are then sequenced; EBI description explicitly contrasts 'susceptible...isolates with their...resistant mutants for genomic comparison.' AMR_STUDY=mixed (gradeable): deposited set is a deliberate two-category design — colistin-susceptible OXA-48-producing clinical parental isolates vs their lab-selected colistin-resistant stable mutants, per EBI description. AMR_TARGET=carbapenem/partial: primary clinical isolate selection criterion was OXA-48 production (carbapenemase=carbapenem resistance); mutant selection was for colistin resistance (not enumerated as carbapenem/3GC, would be 'other'); two distinct targets per category — 'carbapenem' reflects only the parental clinical selection. AMR_METHOD=not_gradeable: method of OXA-48 detection in clinical lab not stated by paper (PCR or other molecular method implied but not named); mutants selected by PAP assay (phenotypic, would be ast_result); two different methods for two categories and parental method is not specified. HOST: only 9 parental isolates originate from human patients; 45 mutants are in vitro-selected and must be left blank per rubric — applies_whole_project false; proposed_value 'human' covers the parental subset only. ISOLATION_SOURCE: specimen types for parental clinical isolates not stated ('samples of different patients' only); mutants are in vitro selections (must be blank per rubric); no single value assignable. COUNTRY: all three collection hospitals are in Spain → applies_whole_project true. COLLECTION_DATE: no collection dates mentioned in the paper.

raw.notes: SIZING: ENA=54 matches paper exactly: 9 parental clinical isolates + 5 PAP-selected colistin-resistant mutants per parental = 45 mutants; 9+45=54. Paper coverage = 100%. STUDY_TYPE: Classified experimental_evolution because 45/54 (83%) deposited sequences are in vitro-selected colistin-resistant mutants derived by culturing clinical isolates on colistin-containing agar (PAP assay), constituting deliberate antibiotic-pressure selection of resistant derivatives that are then sequenced; EBI description explicitly contrasts 'susceptible...isolates with their...resistant mutants for genomic comparison.' AMR_STUDY=mixed (gradeable): deposited set is a deliberate two-category design — colistin-susceptible OXA-48-producing clinical parental isolates vs their lab-selected colistin-resistant stable mutants, per EBI description. AMR_TARGET=carbapenem/partial: primary clinical isolate selection criterion was OXA-48 production (carbapenemase=carbapenem resistance); mutant selection was for colistin resistance (not enumerated as carbapenem/3GC, would be 'other'); two distinct targets per category — 'carbapenem' reflects only the parental clinical selection. AMR_METHOD=not_gradeable: method of OXA-48 detection in clinical lab not stated by paper (PCR or other molecular method implied but not named); mutants selected by PAP assay (phenotypic, would be ast_result); two different methods for two categories and parental method is not specified. HOST: only 9 parental isolates originate from human patients; 45 mutants are in vitro-selected and must be left blank per rubric — applies_whole_project false; proposed_value 'human' covers the parental subset only. ISOLATION_SOURCE: specimen types for parental clinical isolates not stated ('samples of different patients' only); mutants are in vitro selections (must be blank per rubric); no single value assignable. COUNTRY: all three collection hospitals are in Spain → applies_whole_project true. COLLECTION_DATE: no collection dates mentioned in the paper.

notes: SIZING (Scenario C): ENA reports 50 Klebsiella-taxon samples (all 50 total ENA samples), yet the paper describes only 12 Klebsiella isolates (8 CPE: 6 K. pneumoniae + 2 K. oxytoca; 4 non-CPE: 4 K. pneumoniae) out of 90 total Enterobacteriaceae. Paper Klebsiella coverage = 12/50 = 24%, well below 75%. This likely reflects ENA taxonomy reclassifying some deposited Enterobacter or other genera under Klebsiella, rather than a true umbrella accession, since DRA008386 maps directly to this single paper. Study-level attributes are graded gradeable only where supported by the EBI title/description. The EBI title ('Multicenter clinical and molecular epidemiological analysis of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae in Japan') supports Japan, hospital/clinical setting, CRE (AMR) selection, and carbapenem target. AMR method (ast_result) is additionally supported because 'carbapenem-resistant' in the EBI title denotes a phenotypic MIC-based classification, not gene detection. cohort_age is not_gradeable: EBI title/description does not specify age and coverage is too low; although the paper's patient ages (CPE median 77 IQR 69-82, non-CPE median 70 IQR 61-79) point exclusively to adults, one of 11 participating centers is a Pediatrics department, and the 38 ENA Klebsiella not covered by the paper cannot be confirmed. Isolation source is genuinely mixed across sputum, urine, blood, bile, intra-abdominal, wound, and stool; no single source reaches ~95% predominance.

study_setting.evidence_quote: An extensively drug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical isolate was exposed to various antibiotics in vitro. This isolate was sequenced after 20 days of selective pressure to identify variations contributing to resistance.

coverage_basis: Two colonies from day 0 initial isolate plus four colonies from each of four replicates across three treatment groups (CST, PMB, OctC4): 2 + (4 x 4 x 3) = 50, matching the ENA total of 50 exactly.

country.evidence_quote: Institute for Molecular Bioscience, University of Queensland, Brisbane, Australia

isolation_source.evidence_quote: A single colony of 20_GR_12 was selected and grown overnight at 37°C, shaking at 220 rpm. This culture was grown to log phase and plated into three separate 96-well polystyrene, non-treated plates with colistin, polymyxin B or octapeptin C4.

notes: EXCLUDED: experimental_evolution. A single XDR K. pneumoniae ST258 clinical isolate (20_GR_12, sourced from Hygeia General Hospital, Athens, Greece) was serially passaged in vitro under increasing antibiotic concentrations (colistin, polymyxin B, octapeptin C4) for 20 days to induce resistance mutations — a textbook serial-passage resistance-evolution experiment. All 50 ENA-deposited samples are in vitro lab-derived: 2 colonies from the day-0 parental strain plus 4 colonies from each of 4 replicates in each of 3 treatment groups (4×4×3=48), totalling 50, matching the ENA count exactly. Paper coverage = 100%. Because all sequenced isolates are in vitro evolved cultures, isolation_source and host are left null per rubric. study_setting, amr_study, cohort_age are not_gradeable as the standard clinical-study categories do not apply. Country is Australia (University of Queensland, Brisbane), the institution where the in vitro experiments were conducted; the original clinical source isolate was from Greece but that isolate itself is not among the 50 deposited records.
